title: Within-hand grip variability did not improve walking-difficulty prediction across two NHANES releases
abstract: In adults aged40+ with complete bilateral maximal-effort grip measurements, adding within-hand three-trial coefficients of variation to age, sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, combined maximal grip and bilateral asymmetry did not improve prediction of health-related difficulty walking without equipment. A model trained in NHANES2011–2012 (n=2741) was frozen and tested in separately sampled2013–2014 (n=3002). Weighted Brier gain was -0.0002050 (source/target PSU-refit95% interval -0.0016854 to 0.0006234); positive denotes improvement. This scoped negative result does not establish absence of physiological information or prospective clinical utility.
